We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace. You will thrive in dynamic environments, enjoy tackling challenges beyond your comfort zone, and be excited to contribute across the business. In return, we’ll provide the support and opportunities you need to grow and excel as a lawyer. You’ll be part of a legal team that is highly respected within both the company and the broader legal industry—committed to excellence, collaboration, and making a meaningful impact. jobs.title: Director, EMEA Government Affairs & Public Policy
jobs.description: Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake. Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital. The role in a nutshell: Our customers include some of the most regulated organizations in the world, and we have a strong and growing UK and European customer base. Europe is one of our highest-growth priorities. It is also where the rules for our category are actively being written — the Cyber Resilience Act, NIS2, the EU AI Act, and the standards work running underneath all of them. We are hiring our first dedicated European government affairs and public policy leader to own that ground. You will set Chainguard’s European policy strategy, establish us as a trusted technical voice with the officials and bodies shaping cyber regulation on the continent and in the UK, and translate fast-moving policy into what it means for our positioning, our product, and our customers. What you'll do Set and own Chainguard’s European policy strategy — priorities, positions, target institutions and officials, and the narrative we take into the policy process. Engage governments, regulators, and standards bodies across Europe and the UK, including the European Commission (notably DG CNECT and DG GROW), the European Parliament, ENISA, and the standards bodies — CEN-CENELEC and ETSI — doing the technical work underneath the CRA and NIS2. Assist with the Privacy by Design program supporting product development and modification, including software and AI use cases. Collaborate with Vendor Management on vendor qualification and on implementation of Data Processing Agreements and Transfer Impact Assessments as applicable. Research and review country-specific data privacy frameworks and regulations to support continued compliance and business opportunities. Collaborate cross-functionally to implement technical and organizational measures that support data privacy. Monitor how personal data is collected, processed, and stored for compliance with applicable laws. Participate in investigations and impact assessments related to information security events with privacy implications. Serve as a backup point of contact for data protection authorities and data subjects, handling inquiries and requests. Collaborate cross-functionally to improve data privacy processes in support of risk management frameworks such as GDPR and HIPAA. Maintain clear documentation of privacy activities and support audit and regulatory readiness as assigned. Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience (required).
